{{More footnotes|date=August 2020}}

In the mathematical field of [[functional analysis]], a '''nuclear C*-algebra''' is a [[C*-algebra]] {{mvar|A}} such that for every C*-algebra {{mvar|B}} the [[Injective tensor product|injective]] and [[Projective tensor product|projective]] C*-[[cross norm]]s coincides on the algebraic tensor product {{math|''A''⊗''B''}} and the completion of {{math|''A''⊗''B''}} with respect to this norm is a C*-algebra. This property was first studied by {{harvtxt|Takesaki|1964}} under the name "Property T", which is not related to [[Kazhdan's property T]].

==Characterizations==
Nuclearity admits the following equivalent characterizations:
* The identity map, as a [[completely positive map]], approximately factors through matrix algebras. By this equivalence, nuclearity can be considered a [[noncommutative topology|noncommutative]] analogue of the existence of [[partitions of unity]].
* The [[enveloping von Neumann algebra]] is [[Von Neumann algebra#Amenable von Neumann algebras|injective]].
* It is [[Amenable Banach algebra|amenable]] as a [[Banach algebra]].
* ('''For separable algebras''') It is isomorphic to a C*-subalgebra {{mvar|B}} of the [[Cuntz algebra]] {{math|𝒪<sub>2</sub>}} with the property that there exists a [[conditional expectation]] from {{math|𝒪<sub>2</sub>}} to {{mvar|B}}.  

== Examples ==
The commutative unital C* algebra of (real or complex-valued) [[continuous functions]] on a [[compact space|compact]] [[Hausdorff space]] as well as the noncommutative unital algebra of {{math|''n''×''n''}} real or complex matrices are nuclear.<ref><!--Per [[WP:RS/Perennial sources#Stack_Exchange]], StackExchange answers are disfavored as self-published sources.
